chunks: “If a Muslim kills a Christian, and the family of the Christian wishes to kill him, they may kill him, and they must pay the excess of the difference between the two blood-monies.”

Because the proper way regarding these narrations is that we interpret them as applying to one who habitually kills the People of dhimmah. Whoever is like that, then the Imam may, at that point, have him killed, and the family of the dhimmi shall pay the excess of the blood-money of the Muslim over that of the dhimmi to his heirs. This is only done so that others may be deterred from killing the People of dhimmah, and what indicates that is what he narrated:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Abi al-Mi'za, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: protected non-Muslim subjects living under Muslim rule
key_terms.الدِّيَتَيْنِ: the two blood-monies whose difference must be paid
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيَّ: a Christian victim mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the legitimate authority who may enforce the ruling
key_terms.وَرَثَتِهِ: the heirs of the person subject to the ruling
key_terms.يَرْتَدِعَ: be deterred or restrained from committing such an act

ai.seo_question: How are Shia hadiths understood regarding a Muslim who kills a Christian from the People of dhimmah?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a legal ruling concerning retaliation for the killing of a Christian by a Muslim, along with payment of the difference between the two blood-monies. It further explains that such reports are to be understood in the case of one who habitually kills protected non-Muslims, where the Imam may enforce execution as a deterrent.
